findings.cross_file_justification: The catalog writer is not in the diff. The new test asserts on a specific human-readable comment line inside the written YAML text, which indicates the tool edits model-config.yaml line-by-line as text rather than round-tripping through a YAML dumper. The docstring hunk in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py documents that free-text values (--host-route, cli_version read from the CLI, cli_model, transport) are written into the ceiling_calibration block. If those strings are interpolated unquoted, a value containing a newline, `: `, or `#` changes the YAML structure of a file cheval relies on for routing and ceilings.
findings.description: The headless transport writes operator-supplied (--host-route) and CLI-reported (cli_version) free text into model-config.yaml via textual line edits. Neither the diff nor the tests show quoting/escaping of those values, and no test exercises a host-route or cli_version containing YAML-significant characters.
findings.failure_mode: A host route or CLI version string containing a newline or colon injects additional keys (e.g., an overriding effective_input_ceiling or a different model entry) into the catalog, or produces a file that fails to parse and takes cheval down at load time. Because the write is atomic and the record claims written_ceiling, the corruption is silent until the next consumer reads the catalog.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize every written scalar with yaml.safe_dump(value, default_style='"').strip() or an equivalent quoting routine, reject values containing \n or \r before the first paid call (alongside the existing pre-flight prerequisite checks), and add a test writing a host route like `x: 1\neffective_input_ceiling: 1` that asserts the parsed catalog is unchanged apart from the intended fields.

findings.description: `--write-partial-as-operator-set` writes a budget-capped, unbracketed measurement under `source: operator_set`. The schema test explicitly asserts `probe_outcome` is NOT required, so nothing forces consumers or future writers to carry the provenance distinction. A consumer that branches on `source` alone treats the partial value as an operator-vouched calibration with the operator's stale_after_days window.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream staleness and trust logic keyed on `source == operator_set` accepts a machine-produced partial bound as hand-verified evidence. The written value is a verified lower bound, so the direct risk is mis-attribution rather than an oversize ceiling, but the audit trail no longer distinguishes vouched-from-probe from hand-set.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `probe_outcome` required whenever `method` is `probed_headless` (schema `if/then`), or write such entries under a distinct source such as `operator_set_from_partial_probe`. Add a schema test that a `probed_headless` entry without `probe_outcome` is rejected.

findings.description: The record JSON and stderr carry raw provider error bodies (`detail`, 300 chars), OS error strings with paths (`error`: 'catalog not written ... No space left'), the interrupting exception text (`interrupted`), and for non-^C exceptions a full Python traceback including local function names. Probe records are evidence artifacts that are likely committed alongside the catalog change.
findings.failure_mode: Provider error bodies from Bedrock or the Anthropic API can include account/route identifiers, ARNs, request IDs or quota details; tracebacks reveal local filesystem layout. Committing the record publishes these to anyone with repo access.
findings.suggested_fix: Redact known identifier patterns (ARNs, request IDs, absolute home paths) before storing `detail`/`error`/`interrupted`, keep the full traceback on stderr only (not in the record), and document that records may contain provider diagnostics before being committed.

findings.description: This test invokes the real `main()` with `--transport claude-headless --budget-usd 20 --max-tokens-probe 400000` and no `fake` fixture. It is only safe because the `tool` fixture (not shown in this part of the diff) is expected to point CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN at the non-existent sentinel `loa-probe-no-real-cli`. The test's own assertion depends on that sentinel string appearing in the error.
findings.failure_mode: If the fixture's env setup is reordered, removed, or the tool gains a PATH fallback to `claude`, a routine `pytest` run on a developer host with a working claude-bedrock wrapper spawns real 100K-400K token requests and spends real money up to the $20 cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Set CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to the sentinel explicitly inside this test via monkeypatch.setenv, and have the tool refuse to run the headless transport when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is unset or not an absolute path (usage error, exit 2) so there is no PATH-lookup fallback.
